The `sha256sums` array contains a valid checksum, indicating intent to verify the source (though verification occurs later, not during `--printsrcinfo`). There are no top-level shell commands, `curl`/`wget` invocations, `eval` calls, or data exfiltration attempts present in the global scope.

Since sourcing this PKGBUILD for `--printsrcinfo` does not trigger any active code execution beyond safe variable declarations, it poses no immediate risk during this phase. Any potentially risky behavior (if present) would reside inside the build functions, which are out of scope for this narrow gate and will be audited separately.
</details>
